Deprecated. Going with 84691: Implement padded log entry based log rotation | https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/openpower-vpd-parser/+/84691
please check my comments
should we flush() to make sure line is written to file immediately ?

Why do we want the data to be written to file immediately? These log files are only going to be used by humans, when a dump is generated. No other process is waiting for data to be written to the file. In any case, this comment is related to code which has not changed in this patch set?
agree, as no other process is waiting for data to be written to the file.
we are not capturing what is the exception.
This comment is on code which has not changed in this patch set? We can maybe file a github issue and take this up later.
Created https://github.com/openbmc/openpower-vpd-parser/issues/16 to track this.

should we close m_fileStream, in case of exception ?
eg: in case exception occurred while renaming or opening a file from rotateFile().
and what is the mechanism in case of failure for next logging as m_fileStream is not valid any more ?
This comment is related to code which has not changed in this patch set? We can maybe file a github issue and take this up later.
Created https://github.com/openbmc/openpower-vpd-parser/issues/16 to track this.
can we keep this in constants, so developer will know and void using this file path in vpd-manager ?
Done
filesystem::rename itself deletes new file if exists already.
Done
should we close m_fileStream before renaming.
Done

why another logger instance? we got one in 241.
AM I missing something?
Done
failbit & badbit are not set.
Done
don't you think we should open it inside if(file_exists ?) block? line 337
No. The check file exists check on line 337 before opening the file is meant to see if there is an existing file, and rotate it if needed (line 349).
NOT seeing use of m_fileStream?
It's used in other APIs in `logger.cpp`
Done
can we make use of earlier opened stream - m_fileStream?
No. `m_fileStream` is for writing log data to file. `l_readFileStream` is for reading number of lines from the file.

The commit seems to be doing more than what is mentioned in the commit message.
Should this be broken further into multiple individual commits?

>The commit seems to be doing more than what is mentioned in the commit message.

Can you elaborate this?
Other than file rotation, Constructor of the interface appears to be moved and modified. I don't see any explanation about that in the commit message.
Split out the constructor part into patch https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/openpower-vpd-parser/+/84655/1
But why there is such requirement?
The requirement came from stakeholders. If I have to guess, its to put a maximum limit on the size of the log file so that it (and subsequently size of BMC dump) doesn't increase infinitely.

>  its to put a maximum limit on the size of the log file so that it (and subsequently size of BMC dump) doesn't increase infinitely.

This is what should be part of commit messages as well. This is what I was looking for. "What" and "Why"
Addressed this.
a relevant file name? Like write_vpd.log or something like that?

We cannot have a common temporary file, since we have an instance of `SyncFileLogger` and `AsyncFileLogger`, if both instances hit `rotateFile()`, there will be a conflict. Hence, keeping the temporary file name as `m_filePath_temp.log`
in case of error, we quietly returning from the API, caller is continuing writing to existing file. should we handle this scenario ?

Incase of error here, the current log message will be added to existing file, so the current log message is not lost. When the next `logMessage()` is called, `rotateFile()` will be triggered and we will re-try rotating the file.
In case of failure, we continue open and write to old file(which exceeds max lines). Is this expected behaviour ?

Incase of error here, the current log message will be added to existing file, so the current log message is not lost. When the next `logMessage()` is called, `rotateFile()` will be triggered and we will re-try rotating the file.
